sources: https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234512 (facility record, notices, rate table, campsite catalog, availability Nov 2026 - Sept 2027)

values.note: $29 a night in the peak season (2026: May 1 - Sept 19; 2027: Apr 30 - Sept 18), $20 off-peak and first-come. Fees drop 25% when the water is off. One vehicle included; extra vehicles $8 a night.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234512/rates (Peak 2026-05-01..09-19 and 2027-04-30..09-18 STANDARD NONELECTRIC 29; Non-Peak and First-come seasons 20) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/recreation/ansel-watrous-campground ('Peak Season Single Site: $29 per night / Non-Peak Season Single Site: $20 per night'; 'Fees are discounted 25% when water is off') + recreation.gov notice ('Any additional vehicles will be charged $8.00 per vehicle per night'), read 2026-10-26

hookups.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 234512 (all 17 sites NONELECTRIC) + notice ('No RV water connections are available. Come with your RV/trailer water tank filled.'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Upper loop sites 1-7 (back-in, 36-40 ft; FS: spurs 25-45 ft) plus walk-to sites 8-10; lower loop sites 11-17 (back-in, 33 ft; 14 is tent-only). The lower loop is not for trailers over 20 ft (a hairpin switchback at its entrance); the FS page gives the lower loop a 30-ft overall limit. Sites 8, 9, 10 and 14 fit one vehicle only.

sites.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 234512 (17 sites: UPPER 001-010, LOWER 011-017; max vehicle length 33-40, all Back-In) + notices ('The campground's lower loop is not accessible to trailers longer than 20 feet, due to a hairpin switchback near the campground entrance. The parking length ranges from 25 to 45 feet in upper loop.') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/recreation/ansel-watrous-campground ('In the lower loop RV size is limited to an overall length of 30 feet.'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Hand-pump drinking water until Sept 28; filling RV tanks at the hydrants is not allowed. Firewood from the host. Bear lockers at the tent-pad sites.

facilities.source: recreation.gov facility record ('Vault toilets and drinking water are provided'; amenities 'Drinking Water (Hand Pump)'; notices 'Drinking water is available at the campground until Sept. 28th each year', 'Filling at campground hydrants ... is not allowed') + FS page ('Vault toilet(s)', 'Potable water is available at this site'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: The upper loop is open year-round; the lower loop May 1 - Sept 20.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/recreation/ansel-watrous-campground ('The upper loop of the campground is open year-round.') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/conditions (status table: 'Lower: May 1 - Sept 20 / Upper: OPEN year-round'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Upper sites 2, 3, 6, 7 and walk-to sites 8-10 take reservations all year (recreation.gov shows them bookable Nov 2026 - Mar 2027); upper sites 1, 4, 5 and lower site 11 are first-come only, and the lower loop is reservable only in its May - September season. Book at least 4 days ahead; a reserved site must be occupied within 26 hours of its start or it is let first-come. Max 8 people per site.

booking.source: recreation.gov availability for 234512 (Nov 2026, Jan/Mar 2027: sites 002/003/006 'Available'; 001/004/005 'Not Reservable' every month; lower loop 'Closed' Nov - Apr) + rules ('reservationCutOff 4 day(s) prior to arrival') + notices ('All campsites must be occupied within 26 hours of the beginning of the reservation'; 'All sites are available on a first-come, first-served basis before and after the reservation season'), read 2026-10-26

note: Canyon Lakes Ranger District, Arapaho-Roosevelt NF: in Ponderosa pines on the bank of the Cache la Poudre (a Wild and Scenic River) in Poudre Canyon, 24 mi from Fort Collins on Hwy 14. EKKO belongs in the upper loop; the lower loop's entrance has a hairpin switchback. --Claude
summary: recreation.gov (record, rates, catalog, availability) + FS page + status table: confirmed $20-29, no hookups, 17 sites, max 40 ft; added no water/sewer hookups, back-in only, vault toilets + hand-pump water, upper loop open (and partly reservable) year-round, lower May 1 - Sept 20, 180-day window, 4-day cutoff, some first-come sites. Note: dropped '17 sites, sites to ~40 ft' and 'Reservable online'.
flags: Entry phone is empty. Canyon Lakes Ranger District 970-295-6600 (FS page); recreation.gov lists 970-295-6700 and '(530) 529-0578' for facility-specific information.
Site count conflict: the forest's status table says 19 sites and 30' max spur; recreation.gov's catalog has 17 (13 standard, 3 walk-to, 1 tent-only). Kept 17.

Lower-loop length conflict: recreation.gov says trailers over 20 ft cannot reach the lower loop (hairpin); the FS page says lower-loop RVs are limited to 30 ft overall. Either way the upper loop (spurs 25-45 ft) takes a 23-ft motorhome, so the entry passes.
FS agency page for the website field: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/arp/recreation/ansel-watrous-campground
